market_summary: US stock markets are being driven by AI semiconductor developments and regulatory scrutiny. Nvidia released its Open Agent Safety Platform on Sept 28 to address AI safety concerns, while DeepSeek's partnership with Huawei to develop alternative AI chip programming tools signals intensifying competition for Nvidia's dominance. Apple's iPhone 18 Pro posted strong 12% YoY sales growth in China's launch week, capturing 33% smartphone market share despite price increases. Amazon and Apple face a UK class action lawsuit over marketplace restrictions. US equities and tech stocks remain volatile amid these competing pressures. Singapore's financial stocks are performing well, with STI up 24.6% YTD driven by bank rallies following September rate hike prospects. SGX CEO compensation increased 7.1% to S$8.37 million in FY2026 amid a standout year for the exchange.

items.headline: Nvidia launches Open Agent Safety Platform with 100+ industry partners
items.summary: <cite index="2-1">Nvidia released the Open Agent Safety Platform on September 28, a set of tools meant to stop AI agents from causing security problems when they act on their own.</cite> <cite index="3-5">The platform was introduced with over 100 industry partners.</cite>

items.headline: DeepSeek partners with Huawei to develop alternative chip programming tools, reducing reliance on Nvidia
items.summary: <cite index="11-1">DeepSeek partnered with Huawei Technologies to develop programming tools for Huawei's Ascend chips, amid a growing push among Chinese tech firms to seek alternatives to Nvidia.</cite> <cite index="14-3">The tools include TileLang, China's answer to Nvidia's CUDA.</cite>

items.headline: iPhone 18 Pro sales rise 12% YoY in China launch week; Apple captures 33% market share
items.summary: <cite index="20-4">Sales of the new iPhone 18 Pro models in their first three days after launching on September 18 were 12 per cent higher than sales of the iPhone 17 Pro line-up during its entire first week last year.</cite> <cite index="20-5">Apple captured 33 per cent of the market in the week of September 14 to 20.</cite>

items.headline: UK tribunal allows class action suit against Amazon and Apple to proceed on marketplace restrictions
items.summary: <cite index="29-1">Amazon and Apple were told on September 28 that part of a consumer class action against them can proceed, after a ruling by Britain's Competition Appeal Tribunal.</cite> <cite index="29-2">The surviving portion of the claim is valued at between £289 million and £306 million, including interest.</cite>

items.headline: SGX CEO Loh Boon Chye's pay rises 7.1% to S$8.37 million in FY2026
items.summary: <cite index="45-10">The STI hit a record 5,801.96 in early September, with DBS, OCBC, and UOB posting weekly gains of 3–4% as markets priced in the hike.</cite> SGX's CEO compensation rose as the exchange delivered strong results.

items.headline: UOB loses $1.9 million claim against Stamford Land over rights issue
items.summary: Stamford Land won a $1.9 million claim against UOB over rights issue, after the bank was found grossly negligent.
